To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Vitronectin is associated with sites of cell-subsubstrate contact in cultures of myotubes and myofibroblasts.
vitronectins are present at all sites where cells attach to a substrate, but that their antigenic sites are masked by other macromolecules.
vitronectins are present at sites of cell substrate contact, but are masked by other molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the extracellular matrix molecules involved in the attachment of cells to the substrate, and with the role of these molecules in the formation of cell-substrate contacts.
the role of vitronectin in cell-substrate adhesion and cell migration, and with the mechanisms by which cells attach to the substrate and migrate.
the study of the cell surface and its relationship to the substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vitronectin molecule is present at the cell surface in all regions where cells are in contact with a substrate, but the antigenic sites are not exposed at the cell surface.
the antigenic sites of vitronectin are obscured by material from the cell and/or the glass, and that vitronectins are present at all sites where cells attach to the glass.
vitronectins are present in the ECM of the myotube, and that they are not present in the ECM at the focal contacts of the fibroblasts, or at the broad adhesion sites of the myotubes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitronectins are present at all sites where cells are attached to a substrate.
vitronectins are present in the extracellular matrix, and are involved in cell adhesion.

the vitronectin in the extracellular matrix is not involved in the formation of focal contacts or adhesion plaques, but may be associated with the extracellular matrix at the cell surface in a manner that is not dependent on cell-substrate contact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma membrane is not the only component of the cell-substrate junction.
the plasma membrane is the only barrier to diffusion of vitronectin to the glass substrate, which suggests that vitronectins are not the primary components of focal contacts.
, in the case of the myotubes, the broad adhesion plaque is not an isolated structure, but a region of close contact that is continuous with the surrounding areas.
